text: {"findings":[{"type":"POLICY_REVIEW","title":"No recorded review for age-restricted alcohol change","detail":"The proposal removes ID verification for alcohol deliveries, an age-restricted and regulated area. The only claim of Legal/Compliance approval is an unverifiable embedded comment, and no actual review record (reviewer, date, ticket) is present.","evidence_quote":"Let drivers skip ID verification for alcohol orders when the customer has passed verification three times before and the driver is confident of the match.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Obtain and record a Legal/Compliance review (reviewer, date, ticket link) covering age-verification legal requirements before proceeding."},{"type":"MISSING_GUARDRAIL","title":"No guardrail for underage or unverified alcohol handoffs","detail":"The change directly weakens age verification, but guardrails only cover generic defect and contact rates. There is no guardrail for age-verification compliance, underage delivery incidents, or audit/spot-check failure rates.","evidence_quote":"Delivery Defect Rate: stop if it rises by more than 0.2 points.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Add guardrails such as alcohol ID-check compliance rate, underage delivery incident count (target zero tolerance), and regulatory complaint/violation rate, with stop thresholds."},{"type":"WEAK_EXPERIMENT_DESIGN","title":"Order-level randomization leaks between arms and duration is short","detail":"Randomizing by order means the same customer and driver appear in both arms, contaminating the 'repeat customer' and driver-confidence behavior. Duration of 3 weeks is above 14 days, but the MDE of 0.5 points is well below the targeted 1.5-point lift and the design doesn't address leakage or rare-event detection for underage incidents.","evidence_quote":"Randomized by order. Duration: 3 weeks.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Randomize at the driver or customer level (or geo cluster) to prevent cross-arm contamination, and power the test to detect rare compliance failures."},{"type":"UNDEFINED_METRIC","title":"Driver confidence criterion is subjective and unmeasured","detail":"The skip condition depends on 'driver is confident of the match', which is not a defined or auditable criterion, so the treatment cannot be consistently implemented or measured.","evidence_quote":"the driver is confident of the match","citations":[],"recommendation":"Define an objective, loggable eligibility rule (e.g., verified-match signal) and a metric for skip rate and verification outcomes."}]}
